blocks.text: Aguas Calientes: the riverside promenade in a mountain valley

After breakfast, spend the day in Cusco at your own pace. Walk through the old streets, visit museums, shop for souvenirs or take a break at a café.

If you’d like to get out of the city, you can choose from two optional excursions.

The full-day Sacred Valley trip costs $220 per person.

In Pisac, you’ll visit a craft market selling ceramics and goods made from wool, silver and leather. At the Awanakancha centre, you’ll see llamas, alpacas, guanacos and vicuñas and learn how wool is processed and coloured with natural dyes.

In Ollantaytambo, explore the archaeological site with its monumental terraces, stone structures and remains of fortifications. You’ll see Andean valleys between stops and learn about Inca heritage and local crafts along the way.

Lunch is a buffet at a restaurant serving Peruvian cuisine. Return to Cusco for an overnight stay at Xima Cusco 4★ or a similar hotel.

The trip to Vinicunca Rainbow Mountain takes a full day. The group excursion with an English-speaking guide costs $55 per person. A private trip with an English-speaking guide costs $200 per person for groups of two or more.

The coloured bands on the slopes come from mineral layers, with red, yellow, green and white rock side by side. Vinicunca is about 100 km from Cusco, in Quispicanchi Province. The route reaches about 5,200 m. From the mountain, you can see nearby ridges and Ausangate, a peak sacred to the Incas.

Departure is around 04:00, with a return to Cusco at approximately 19:00. Breakfast and lunch are included. You’ll need good stamina at this altitude. If you’d like to ride a horse for part of the ascent, hire costs $40.

Overnight at Xima Cusco 4★ or a similar hotel.
